resale_co.name: Certificate of Compliance (change of tenancy, use or ownership)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Allendale Construction Code Official, with the Property Maintenance Official, Zoning Official and the Borough Fire Inspector
resale_co.lead_time: The Code says the inspection is made within 10 to 15 days of receiving the application and fee, and not more than 60 days before the change of ownership.
resale_co.valid_for: Inspection may be made no more than 60 days before the change of ownership
requirements: Inspection of the visual parts of the house for Borough code violations, with no pending violations or orders from the Construction, Property Maintenance or Zoning Officials
Smoke alarms on each level and within 10 feet of each sleeping area (10-year sealed battery units where battery powered); carbon monoxide alarms; listed in the application
Portable fire extinguisher 2A-10B:C within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)
A low voltage smoke alarm system used as the primary system must have been inspected by a qualified technician within 12 months; proof shown to the Fire Inspector
Zoning inspection: pool fence and self-latching gates, visual exterior check, sidewalks (trip hazards must be replaced before closing), house number visible, no open building permits
List any deck, fence, garage, shed, pool or finished basement on the application

fees.label: Certificate of compliance for change in ownership of residential premises (Zoning fee schedule, Code Section 120-23)
fees.quote: Certificate of compliance for change in tenancy, use or ownership of residential premises, pursuant to §270-103 $100

fees.label: Certificate of occupancy for change in ownership of nonresidential or residential premises (separate line in the same schedule; which one applies to a home sale is unclear)
fees.quote: Certificate of occupancy for change in tenancy, use or ownership of nonresidential or residential premises, pursuant to §270-103 $200

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online with the Borough's Certificate of Compliance application (GovPilot), listed on the Construction and Zoning Permits & Forms page, and pay in full before the application is reviewed. Give the closing date, new owner details and who to contact for the inspection. The Construction Code Office (500 W Crescent Ave) is open Monday to Friday 9:00am to 4:30pm.

evidence.quote: No residential or nonresidential property may be changed in tenancy, use or ownership unless a certificate of compliance has been issued by the Borough Construction Code Official on forms provided and the required fee paid for such inspection.
The Construction Official, or his designee, shall inspect any residential or nonresidential property not more than 60 days prior to the change in any tenancy, use or ownership.
Except for a nonresidential structure, the certificate of compliance shall also establish that smoke detectors have been installed pursuant to Chapter 128, Fire Prevention, §128-12.

Upon the transfer of title of a dwelling unit accompanied by a change in the occupancy thereof, the seller, landlord or transferor is required to obtain from the Allendale Construction Code Official a certificate of continued occupancy evidencing that the property is in compliance with the provisions of this chapter.

Within 10 to 15 days of the receipt of the application and fee, the designated inspector of the office of the Construction Code Official shall inspect the premises to determine whether the same complies with the provisions of this chapter.
I acknowledge that payment must be made in full before this application will be reviewed
Sidewalks will be inspected cracks and change in elevation that creates trip hazards. They will be required to be replaced prior to closing.
The Construction Code Office hours are Monday through Friday between 9:00am and 4:30pm.

resale_co.notes: Code Sections 270-103, 128-12 to 128-15 and 120-23 were read through the ecode360 print view. Section 270-103C (amended 2012) is the current rule: a Certificate of Compliance is needed for any change of ownership, and it also covers the smoke alarm check. The older Chapter 128 article still calls it a certificate of continued occupancy and points to a fee in Section 100-3A(8)(a) that no longer lists it. The Zoning fee schedule (Section 120-23, amended 2018) lists $100 for a residential certificate of compliance and a separate $200 certificate of occupancy for change of ownership; the GovPilot form's fee schedule did not load, so confirm the amount with the office. Other staff on the Construction and Zoning page: Joann Catalfumo, Building Department Administrative Assistant, ext. 201; Mike Limatola, Technical Assistant, ext. 202. Rental tenancy changes also need the certificate; that is not a sale item.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and within ten feet of each separate sleeping area, listed to ANSI/UL 217; basement alarms near the stairway to the floor above
Ten-year sealed battery smoke alarms where battery powered; hardwired alarms from original construction may not be replaced with battery units; replace alarms older than 10 years
Carbon monoxide alarms (UL 2034) for each separate sleeping area; combination units are acceptable
Portable fire extinguisher 2A-10B:C, no more than 10 pounds, within 10 feet of the kitchen, mounted, serviced and tagged in the past 12 months or with a recent receipt (form still lists it)
Low voltage primary alarm systems need a technician inspection within 12 months

authorities.name: Borough of Allendale (Certificate of Compliance inspection by the Construction Code Office and Borough Fire Inspector; Allendale Fire Prevention Bureau is the LEA)
authorities.lead_time: Inspection within 10 to 15 days of the application and fee (Code Section 128-15); no tiered rush fees were found.

fees.label: Certificate of Compliance (smoke and CO check is part of this certificate)
fees.quote: Certificate of compliance for change in tenancy, use or ownership of residential premises, pursuant to §270-103 $100

authorities.how_to_apply: The smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and extinguisher check is done as part of the Certificate of Compliance; apply with the same online GovPilot application. For fire code questions contact Allendale Fire Prevention.

evidence.quote: Proof of this inspection must be available to the Borough of Allendale Fire Inspector at the time of inspection for the Certificate of Compliance
Except for a nonresidential structure, the certificate of compliance shall also establish that smoke detectors have been installed pursuant to Chapter 128, Fire Prevention, §128-12.
other than owner-occupied one- and two-family dwellings

fire_cert.notes: The state fire directory lists the Borough Building Department (500 W Crescent Av) as the smoke detector compliance office, which matches the Borough code: the smoke/CO check is part of the Certificate of Compliance. Fire Official Kevin M Todd is listed in the state directory (survey 6/4/2025) with phone (201) 818-4400; the Borough page lists ext. 301. Allendale's fire code article excludes owner-occupied 1-2 family homes from routine fire inspections, but that does not affect the sale certificate. The online form still lists a portable fire extinguisher; state law (P.L.2025, c.19) removed it from the sale certificate in February 2025, so confirm.

other_items.label: Final water reading
other_items.detail: Call Suez at (855) 367-6708 for a final water reading 72 hours before closing. Water charges are lienable and must be paid before closing.

other_items.label: Sidewalk inspection
other_items.detail: The zoning inspection checks sidewalks for cracks and trip hazards; failing sections must be replaced before closing.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: Any open building permits are checked during the zoning inspection.

open_questions: Which fee applies to a 1-2 family sale: the $100 certificate of compliance or the $200 certificate of occupancy for change of ownership (both in Code Section 120-23)? The GovPilot fee schedule did not load.
Is there any separate Fire Prevention fee for the smoke/CO part, or a rush fee for short notice?
Does Allendale still require the portable fire extinguisher after P.L.2025, c.19?
How long is the certificate valid if the closing is delayed?
